title: observability-supersession-request.v1
description: A reviewed request to retire logical entries from a private inventory, producing its next version.  This document is PUBLIC and is the reason the supersession workflow can be trusted: the change is expressed entirely in logical vocabulary that ADR-0004 already publishes — target ids and credential-ref names — so it is diffable, reviewable and merged onto protected main before anything reads the private store. The alternative, typing target names into a workflow_dispatch box at run time, is an unversioned unreviewed change, which is the gesture this whole programme exists to remove.  RETIREMENT ONLY, and that is a boundary rather than a first cut. Removing an entry needs only its logical name. ADDING one needs a resolved endpoint or credential binding, which must never pass through public Git or a CI input, so provisioning stays a human operation against the private store and this contract has no field for it.  Single-use by construction: `previous.sha256` names the version being replaced, so re-running an applied request refuses — the stored document no longer hashes to it.

document.description: The private document this request supersedes. Checked against the stored document's own name, so a request aimed at the wrong environment's inventory is refused rather than applied.

sha256.description: The compare-and-set half, and the reason this request cannot be applied twice or applied to a document somebody else has since changed. Read it with `inventory-digest`; it discloses nothing.

storage.description: The CONFIRMED storage shape, carried here so the mutation workflow verifies rather than discovers. An earlier draft detected the shape at run time and then wrote immediately, which is detection rather than confirmation — the same defect as a probe whose result nobody reviews before acting on it. The discovery workflow reports the shape and stops; a human puts it here; the mutation refuses if the store disagrees.  The shape is a choice between two code paths and is not sensitive. Where the shape is `field`, the field NAME is storage layout at a private path and stays a secret rather than appearing here.

shape.description: `data-object`: the document IS the secret's data object. `field`: the document is a JSON string in a single named field.

rationale.description: Why these entries are being retired. Minimum length is deliberate, as everywhere else in these contracts: 'cleanup' is not a reason a reviewer can disagree with. The evidence that a product is provably gone belongs here or in a document this cites.

retire.description: At least one group must be named. An empty request would produce a version bump that changed nothing, which the supersession gate refuses anyway — refusing it here says so at the point a reviewer is reading.

targets.description: Logical target ids. Retiring a target retires its credential binding with it: the two are one entry in the private inventory, and a binding whose credential file has been shredded renders a configuration the evaluator cannot load.
